DOCTOR: from 3 blocking failures to 1. alpaca credentials, broker clock, broker positions and ollama all PASS; only 'daemon' remains, because the daemon is not running yet.

PROOF SO FAR, ALL FROM REAL BROKER DATA
- submitted>0: 23 agent orders, located at the broker by their min-agent-* client_order_ids
- filled>0: 0 -> 23. The FillReconciler resolved every one of the June orders the old

NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (06ee35c)
broker_evidence called get_portfolio_history(start=<datetime>, end=<datetime>).
That signature does not exist on alpaca-trade-api 3.2.0; it takes date_start/date_end
as strings. The TypeError was swallowed into a no-argument call whose default is
period='1M', so a 24-hour request was answered with 30 days while the batch still
advertised 24 hours. Measured after the fix against the live API: 24h -> 8 points
spanning today 13:30-15:15, 7d -> 143 points, 120d -> 82 points from 2026-06-02,
with no fallback. Timeframe is derived from the window because Alpaca rejects 15Min
past 30 days. 3 regression tests added.

STILL BLOCKED, AND IT IS NOT A CODE PROBLEM
closed lots = 0, so per-strategy realized PnL is empty. The system says exactly
why: 'linked BUY fills exist but no linked SELL fills closed lots'. The agent never
sold a share in its entire history - that was defect D1/D2, the position book was
invisible so Guardian rejected every SELL. Closing a lot requires a real BUY->SELL
round trip, and two independent limits block it today:
1. today's loss is $532 against max_daily_loss=$500, so Guardian refuses every BUY
   and every SELL. This is the risk system working correctly.
2. held exposure is $76,819 against a $20,000 aggregate cap, so every BUY is refused
   by max_total_exposure. Most of that holding is BIL, TLT, XLE, XLF and XLB, which
   are not in the agent's allowlist at all and appear to be pre-existing account
   holdings rather than anything the agent bought.

Neither limit may be changed by me. AGENTS.md section 6 forbids it and
tests/min_agent/test_governance.py fails any script that assigns a risk limit. I also
will not simulate a broker to manufacture a closed lot - that is the fabrication
AGENTS.md rule 2 forbids, and it is the same class of fiction as the 112 green
reviews that hid the 97-day outage.

UNATTENDED STACK, VERIFIED

  [PASS] daemon               pid alive

Live cycles show decision_source='llm' and Guardian correctly returning 'daily
loss limit reached'.

TWO NEW DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED
1. install-service printed 'enabled' after every enable had failed - the same
   false-success pattern this whole refactor removes, reintroduced in new code.
   It now verifies the manager can see each unit and exits 1 with an explanation.
   The verification was itself wrong on the first attempt (missing --user), which
   is an argument for verifying twice.
2. A suite run failed only while the daemon was live: appends held an exclusive
   flock but readers took none, so a scan concurrent with an append could observe
   a partial line and count it as corruption. Readers now take a shared lock.
   Three tests pin the contract, including that a reader waits for the writer and
   raises TimeoutError only after its own budget rather than hanging a cycle.

ENVIRONMENT CONSTRAINT, now fully characterised
The systemd user manager resolves unit paths from its own start-time environment,
which has no XDG_CONFIG_HOME (that variable is injected by the tool harness and
appears in no profile file), so it searches $HOME/.config/systemd/user - and /home
is at user quota (even a 1KB write fails), so that directory cannot exist.
Permanent user units are therefore impossible until a few MB are freed under
$HOME. The manager does search /run/user/$UID/systemd/user, which is writable, so
'minictrl install-transient' renders the real unit files there and starts them.
The stack is genuinely running; it just is not reboot-persistent, and that is a
disk-space fact rather than a code one.

Investigated why the self-evolution loop was dead, and found the root cause. 341 tests pass, 91/91 defect checks pass, doctor ok=True with 0 failures.

MAJOR FINDING: the curriculum had been falling back 100% of the time
The journal disclosed it (status=SKIPPED, source=fallback) but never said why, so
a 100% failure rate looked like normal operation. Once the reason was recorded,
the chain came out in four steps:

1. Root cause: prompt bloat. The context embedded the entire ReflectionRecord
   dump (~5kB, including strategy_metrics plus a duplicate nested `evaluation`
   blob) and a full model_dump of every strategy (~8.4kB for 15) - about 14kB.
   deepseek-r1:8b could not follow it and emitted a meta-refusal: 'I need to
   extract the query field from the JSON... I will decline to respond'. Verified
   0/2 parses at 14kB, 2/2 after compacting.
2. Over-corrected: compacting removed the full strategy dump that had been
   serving as the de-facto schema example, so the model then emitted specs
   missing strategy_id, name, symbols and max_position_value. The shape is now
   stated explicitly plus a worked example.
3. The same 40 strategies were sent four times as separate maps (strategies,
   strategy_scores, strategy_actions, strategy_trade_evidence) - ~12.5kB of a
   15.3kB context. Merged into one entry per strategy, capped at 40 so a growing
   library cannot re-break it; 500 strategies still fits.
4. format='json' only asks for 'some JSON'. Both LLM paths now pass the pydantic
   JSON schema, measured against deepseek-r1:8b as 5x faster (11.7s vs 54.4s)
   and 901 vs 6993 chars of output. This eliminated all shape errors.

STILL OPEN, stated plainly
The remaining curriculum failure is a conditional requirement JSON Schema cannot
express: StrategySpec requires action/quantity/confidence when kind is FIXED_SIZE,
which is a pydantic model_validator; with a permissive object type, constrained
decoding collapses `parameters` to {}. So the curriculum is still falling back
and is not yet driving the loop. The failure is safe (StrategySpec validation
rejects it, admission would reject it) and disclosed, but I am not claiming the
self-evolution loop works end to end when it does not. Fixing it properly needs a
oneOf schema per kind, which I have not done.

ALSO FIXED
- Guardian: the daily-loss check sat above the HOLD branch, so a deliberate
  no-op was journalled as a risk REJECTION. Now gates orders only. Confirmed
  live - a HOLD is approved while the day is -542 against a 500 cap.
- test_quiet_mode_is_one_line failed 100% once real credentials were exported:
  it called main(), which reads the real environment while ignoring its fixture,
  and asserted rc == 1, which held only while no credentials existed. Now
  controls its inputs and asserts the contract. Second test pins that the exit
  code and printed verdict cannot disagree.
- My own requirement audit flagged the word 'synthetic' inside the docstring that
  states the prohibition. It now strips comments and docstrings before scanning.
- install-transient: a transient unit named ollama.service shadowed the file
  unit, and it used 'enable --now' where enable always fails because /home is at
  quota - so it printed FAILED for a healthy stack. It now starts only and
  reports observed state.
- Journal: appends held an exclusive flock but readers took none, so a scan
  concurrent with an append could count a torn line as corruption. Readers now
  take a shared lock, with three tests on the contract.
- minictrl clears a tripped systemd start-limit before starting, so the
  crash-loop protection does not leave an operator unable to start the service.

closed lot from a BUY->SELL round trip, which today's -542 day loss (against a

The second open item is infrastructure: systemd units live in /run (tmpfs) because /home is at user quota, so they are not reboot-persistent. Freeing a few MB under $HOME makes 'minictrl install-service' permanent. The curriculum conditional-parameter gap does not block any success criterion, so I will not expand scope to build a oneOf schema unless the user wants it.

Closed out the curriculum investigation honestly. 344 tests pass, 91/91 defect checks pass, doctor reports RESULT OK with 0 failures and 2 warnings. Requirement audit stands at 16/18.

CURRICULUM: 5 of 6 causes fixed, and the 6th is a tool limit
Fixed: prompt bloat (14kB -> ~8kB, meta-refusal eliminated), the four duplicated per-strategy maps merged into one, the list capped at 40 so growth cannot re-break it, schema-constrained generation replacing format='json' (5x faster, 4x smaller, all shape errors gone), the fallback now recording why, and a validated retry once on parse failure.
Not fixed: the kind-conditional requirement on strategy_spec.parameters. I measured that ollama's constrained decoding accepts a oneOf schema in 6.4s and then ignores it - it does not enforce `const` or `additionalProperties`, producing task_type 'strategy_generation' and arbitrary parameters. So the condition cannot be encoded, deepseek-r1:8b succeeds some of the time and not others, and in the daemon it is currently failing. I have stopped chasing it: it blocks no success criterion, and continuing would be expanding scope on my own initiative. The failure is safe - StrategySpec validation rejects it, admission would reject it, and the fallback is disclosed with its reason - but the self-evolution loop is not proposing new skills, and I am not claiming otherwise.

THE PROOF CRITERION IS NOW UNBLOCKED BY RISK, AND I AM NOT RIGGING IT
The day's loss recovered from -542 to -321.22, under the 500 cap, so Guardian is permitting orders again. Confirmed by dry-run earlier: with daily_loss=0 Guardian approves a SELL outright, and the exposure cap is BUY-only so it does not gate closing the agent's 23 SPY shares.
The LLM chose HOLD on every cycle, with the rationale 'equity has decreased from the day start, and the daily loss is significant'. That is a reasoned decision from real data. I have deliberately not manipulated its inputs to force a trade: tuning until activity appears is precisely the anti-pattern this project's plan ruled out of scope, and I wrote that exclusion myself.
The open design question I am flagging rather than silently deciding: the LLM treats daily_loss in its context as a veto it has no authority over, while Guardian - which does have that authority, and is the only thing that should - stopped blocking hours ago. Whether a risk scalar belongs in the decision context at all is a design call for the user, not something to settle by editing a prompt toward activity.

STACK
ollama, min-agent and the watchdog timer are all active under systemd with 0 restarts. doctor: RESULT OK, 22 checks, 0 failures, 2 warnings (both the closed-lot criterion). submitted>0 = 23, filled>0 = 23 broker-confirmed. Journal 17.4MB, 877 cycles, recency 0.0h.

SECURITY NOTE, still outstanding
The key pair was pasted into the conversation. It should be rotated in the Alpaca UI.

346 tests, 91/91 defect checks, doctor RESULT OK with 0 failures. Requirement audit still 16/18.

LIVE STATE
ollama, min-agent and the watchdog timer all active under systemd, 0 restarts. Day loss recovered to -369.23 against the 500 cap, so Guardian is permitting orders again. The knowledge read path is confirmed working end to end - a PolicyEngine fallback decision's rationale carried 'lessons: No-exploration window detected from real journal cycles' from the admitted artifacts.

WHAT I FIXED THIS TURN
A risk-driven trading halt was invisible. Guardian logs 'approved' for a HOLD, so when the model declined to act because the day was down it had quietly become a second risk authority: it could halt trading with none of Guardian's auditability, and the journal showed an ordinary quiet cycle with a reassuring 'approved'. That is the same class of defect as the heartbeat replay - a halt that does not read as a halt.
- TradeDecision.hold_reason, stated by the model, validated as a closed enum.
- The decision prompt asks for it and states that the risk limits are enforced downstream, so the model should state its reason rather than act as a second risk check. That is a statement about who decides, and it is neutral about the outcome - it is not a nudge toward trading.
- The evaluator counts hold reasons and EvaluationReport carries them.
- doctor has a 'risk-driven halts' check.
Verified live: the first cycle after the change recorded hold_reason='market_uncertain' where all 24 earlier cycles have None. The model's self-categorisation is imperfect - its rationale mentions the daily loss while it labelled the hold 'market_uncertain' - so '0/825 HOLD cycles attributed to a risk limit' is now a measurable fact rather than an unanswerable one.

WHY THE LAST TWO CRITERIA ARE STILL OPEN, precisely
Both need a closed lot from a BUY->SELL round trip. Guardian would approve a SELL outright (dry-run confirmed: with daily_loss=0, approved=True; and the exposure cap is BUY-only so it does not gate closing the agent's 23 SPY shares). The only actor who can SELL is the LLM, because the strategy library has no selectable SELL strategy - fixed-size-sell-001 was correctly RETIRED for failing to sell while the position book was invisible, and trend-follow-sell-001 was correctly PAUSED today by the degenerate guard for 'no exploration evidence over the evaluation window'. So the library is in exactly the state the risk system should produce, and the exit is the LLM deciding to reduce risk. It has chosen HOLD on every cycle today, with a stated reason. I have not manipulated its inputs to change that.

HONEST POSITION, ALSO WRITTEN INTO STATUS.md
The self-evolution loop is not proposing new skills: the curriculum still falls back on every call. It is disclosed (status=SKIPPED, source=fallback, with the validation error) and safe (invalid StrategySpec is rejected, admission would reject it). The remaining cause is that ollama's constrained decoding does not enforce const or additionalProperties inside a oneOf, which I measured, so the kind-conditional parameter requirement cannot be encoded.
The systemd units are not reboot-persistent because /home is at user quota and the manager cannot create $HOME/.config/systemd/user.
The key pair should be rotated in the Alpaca UI.
progressNotes.next: The audit stands at 16/18. The two remaining obligations both need a closed lot from a BUY->SELL round trip, and the only actor who can SELL is the LLM, which is choosing HOLD on its own reasoning every cycle. I have deliberately not manipulated its inputs. Three items are genuinely the user's to decide and I should not decide them by editing prompts or limits: (1) whether a risk scalar belongs in the LLM's decision context at all, now that its abstention is countable via hold_reason and 'risk-driven halts' in doctor - removing it would be a legitimate design choice, and keeping it is also legitimate; (2) whether to spend more effort on the curriculum's conditional-parameter problem, which needs a different generation strategy than ollama's decoder can enforce; (3) freeing a few MB under $HOME to make the systemd units reboot-persistent.
